outcome: One way to make robots differ: groups say who, set_state and equip say what
owner_impact: Your decision D-023. Initialization now declares who differs with group(...), exact sizes as before (fraction, count or rest), and attaches properties to groups: set_state("informed", informed=1.0) for starting memory, and equip("scouts", "nest", range=5.0) for a reference sensor, whose range the simulator enforces. "all" means every robot. Groups can form independent partitions, like crossed factors: e.g. 20% informed and, independently, 50% equipped, each with exact counts. A robot receiving the same state or sensor from two groups is a compile error. role(...) and the per-robot set_agent_reference_sensor(...) are retired; no Experiment used the latter. Constant Bearing Flocking, its showcase candidate and Firat's aggregation are migrated to groups with the same robots in the same groups as before. Test now: yes. After I tell you the migration is done, republish Constant Bearing Flocking and Firat to the Showcase ('Publish current revision'), then open Constant Bearing Flocking; the setup message should read 'Groups: informed 80, uninformed 120'.
